summary_paragraph: A 30-year-old woman was admitted after reporting suicidal ideation involving a plan to drive into a tree, following a history of bipolar disorder and prior suicide attempts. She was placed under observation with a 1:1 sitter and admitted for monitoring while awaiting electroconvulsive therapy (ECT). Due to poor venous access, a port-a-cath was successfully placed on hospital day 4, with imaging confirming proper placement. Lithium was initiated and titrated to 300 mg nightly for mood stabilization. She remained medically stable throughout her stay, denied active suicidal ideation at discharge, and underwent her first ECT session on the final day. She was discharged to an inpatient psychiatric facility for continuation of ECT and psychiatric care.
problems: Bipolar disorder, current episode depressed, severe, without psychotic features
